label: copy-phase input c echoed at the 2nd or 3rd copy step (original token 0 or 1 is c)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input is the letter c at copy steps recall_idx 1 or 2, i.e. the model is re-reading original token 0 or 1 = c. Magnitude depends strongly on position: when c is the first original token (input right after <DEL>, recall_idx 1) it is strong (~0.8-1.0 of max, 78% of mass); when c is the second original token (recall_idx 2) it is weak (~0.1-0.4 of max). Never fires in the original or delimiter phase, never on any token other than c, and essentially never past recall_idx 2 (a few tiny ~0.03 activations at recall_idx 3). False positives are mostly recall_idx 2 cases in short sequences (L=3-4).

issues: This answers the feature-503 check only. It did not touch the relayed user request about timing batch 2 and launching batch 3.

Most of the claims check out on the dev split. The feature fires only in the copy phase and only when the input is c. Activation share by recall_idx is 0.782 at recall_idx 1 and 0.218 at recall_idx 2, with 12 tiny activations at recall_idx 3. It never fires at to_go 0. recall_idx==1 alone scores precision 1.0, recall 0.529. The reported test scores reproduce: P 0.942, R 0.9997, F1 0.970.

The false positives are systematic, not noise. All of them are c at recall_idx 2 when L <= 4. With L==3 (recall_idx 2 is the last step) the feature never fires: precision 0.0. With L==4 precision is only 0.39. With L>=5, recall_idx 2 has precision 1.0.
The explanation mentions this pattern, but the predicate and label still say 'original token 1 is c' fires for every L. That overclaims. The L>=5 condition is missing.
The 9 test misses are c at recall_idx 3 (~0.01-0.05, 0% of mass) when original tokens 0 and 1 are not c. This is negligible scattered noise.
Adding (L>=5) to the recall_idx 2 term removes every false positive. Test scores go from P 0.942 / F1 0.970 to P 1.0 / R 0.972 / F1 0.986, with mass recall 0.998.
